record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Given an n-component integrable PDE system of the form ∂u/∂t = ξ[u], can one find a differentially non-degenerate n-dimensional Nijenhuis operator L and the BKM parameters described in §2.1 so that, after a local diffeomorphism in the dependent variables u, the system becomes a BKM system?

evidence.quote: That is, given an n-component integrable system of PDEs of the form (7) (or with differential constraints as BKM I and III) found in a literature, can one find a differentially nondegenerate n-dimensional operator L and parameters (1–4) from §2.1 such that the system ‘transforms’ into a BKM system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. On a domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with coordinates $u=(u^1,\dots,u^n)$, a (1,1)-tensor field $L=L^i_j(u)$ is called a Nijenhuis operator if its Nijenhuis torsion
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y)=L^2[X,Y]-L[LX,Y]-L[X,LY]+[LX,LY]$$
vanishes identically. The operator $L$ is called differentially non-degenerate if the coefficients $\sigma_1(u),\dots,\sigma_n(u)$ of its characteristic polynomial $\det(t\cdot\mathrm{Id}-L)=t^n-\sigma_1 t^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^n\sigma_n$ are functionally independent at almost every point (their differentials are linearly independent).
 
BKM data on such an $L$ consist of a choice of: (1) a smooth function $f$ of one variable (defining the "dispersion law"), (2) constants $c_0,c_1,\dots$ entering the construction of conservation laws, (3) a polynomial / rational frame that selects the BKM branch (BKM I, II, or III, possibly with differential constraints), and (4) auxiliary parameters that fix the explicit form of the right-hand side. From these data one builds, by an explicit universal recipe expressed entirely in terms of $L$, $\sigma_i$, and their derivatives, an evolution PDE system
$$\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=\xi_{\text{BKM}}[u]$$
on $\mathbb{R}^n$; such systems are called BKM systems and form an infinite-hierarchy family of integrable PDEs (containing, e.g., KdV, coupled KdV, Harry Dym, Camassa–Holm, Kaup–Boussinesq).

Problem. Let
$$\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=\xi[u]\qquad(u=(u^1,\dots,u^n))$$
be a given $n$-component integrable system of evolutionary PDEs (possibly subject to differential constraints of the BKM I or III type). Develop an effective recognition procedure that decides whether there exist
(a) a differentially non-degenerate $n$-dimensional Nijenhuis operator $L$, and
(b) BKM parameters of types (1)–(4) above,
such that after some local diffeomorphism $u\mapsto \tilde u(u)$ of the dependent variables the system becomes the BKM system associated with $(L,\text{parameters})$. In particular, give checkable necessary and sufficient conditions on $\xi[u]$ for it to be diffeomorphic to a BKM system, and, when they hold, an algorithm to reconstruct $L$ and the parameters.
artifact.category_tag: Nijenhuis geometry and BKM integrable systems
artifact.status_search_result: The recognition problem for BKM systems was posed as an open research direction in late 2024 within the program connecting Nijenhuis geometry to integrable PDE hierarchies. Subsequent works (early-to-mid 2025 and 2026) develop the theory of differentially non-degenerate Nijenhuis operators, finite-gap reductions, jet-density results, and Lax pairs for BKM hierarchies, but none provide a general effective recognition criterion that, given an arbitrary n-component integrable system, decides whether it is diffeomorphic to a BKM system and reconstructs the Nijenhuis operator and BKM parameters. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Given an n-component integrable PDE system, can one find a differentially nondegenerate Nijenhuis operator L and BKM parameters so that the system transforms into a BKM system?
status_evidence.claim: The recognition question is explicitly posed as an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: Almost Differentially Nondegenerate Nijenhuis Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies differentially nondegenerate Nijenhuis operators and extensions thereof.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops foundational theory but does not provide a general BKM recognition algorithm.

status_evidence.title: Jet-density of finite-gap solutions for classes of BKM systems
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes specific subclasses of BKM systems and their solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent follow-up addresses solution structure rather than the inverse recognition problem.
